articles.title: Inside Kestrel and TSMC
articles.abstract: What the fictional Kestrel supply agreement means for N3 allocation next year.
articles.body:
## The deal

Kestrel Semiconductor signed a three-year wafer agreement with TSMC on 12 September 2026, covering 40,000 wafers per quarter.

## Who says so

According to Dana Okafor, a fictional supply-chain analyst, the allocation is the largest N3 commitment by a fabless newcomer.

## The numbers

Kestrel expects gross margin of 52%, capex of $1.2 billion and a 15% rise in unit volume over the term.

The agreement leaves packaging capacity unresolved, which is the open risk for 2027 shipments.

articles.title: N3 capacity is tight
articles.abstract: Why advanced-node slots are scarce this year, in plain terms.
articles.body:
Advanced-node capacity at TSMC is booked well into next year.

Smartphone and accelerator customers compete for the same lines.

New fabs in Arizona and Kumamoto add slots only gradually.

Smaller customers usually wait the longest for allocation.

articles.title: The BoJ widened the band
articles.abstract: My notes on the yield-curve band change and what moved first.
articles.body:
The Bank of Japan widened its tolerance band for ten-year yields this week.

Ten-year JGB yields rose quickly after the announcement.

Life insurers said they would wait before moving money home.

The yen firmed for a day, then gave most of it back.

articles.title: Insurers are patient
articles.abstract: Japanese life insurers and their slow walk back from foreign bonds.
articles.body:
Japanese life insurers hold large foreign bond books.

Hedging costs decide how much of that money comes home.

Most planning documents point to a gradual shift.

A sudden repatriation would need a much steeper curve.

articles.abstract: A synthetic note on advanced packaging lines.
